plan.why: Its Flask server is small, so llocal rewrites it in Go on llocal's kit. A Go server starts in a moment and needs little memory, so the app is quick and can sleep when nobody is using it.
found: An app with its own Flask server.
2 server routes, like GET /api/tickets and POST /api/tickets/{ticket_id}/print.
A SQL Server database at sqlserver01.acme.local.
Addresses on a private network or this computer: 192.168.1.40 (in app.py) and sqlserver01.acme.local (in app.py).

left.text: Its SQL Server database at sqlserver01.acme.local is on a private network, which llocal can't reach to copy the data.
It calls 192.168.1.40 (in app.py) on a private network, which llocal can't reach.
Its data is in SQL Server and moves into one SQLite file beside the app.
Its Flask server (2 routes in 1 file, 1 KB) is rewritten in Go on llocal's kit.
It has no llocal.json yet: the short file that tells llocal how to build and start it.

changes.text: The SQL Server data moves into one SQLite file on llocal, copied over once.
changes.detail: SQLite sits right next to the app, so it is fast, it is backed up with the app, and only people who can open the app reach the data.

changes.text: The Flask server is rewritten in Go on llocal's kit, answering at the same addresses.
changes.detail: A Go server starts in a moment and needs little memory, so the app is quick and can sleep when nobody is using it.

blockers.title: Its database is on a private network
blockers.detail: The SQL Server database at sqlserver01.acme.local can only be reached from inside your network, so llocal cannot copy the data from it.
blockers.way_out: Export the data to a file (a backup, or a spreadsheet per table) and add it to the upload. Or ask whoever runs your network to let llocal's address, 203.0.113.7, reach the database once, for the copy.

warnings: It calls addresses on a private network that llocal cannot reach: 192.168.1.40 (in app.py). Those parts will not work on llocal.
